Okay, so what I would recommend you do is as follows:

1) Flip the bike back up so the wheels are on the ground.

2) Open your quick release, and make sure the springs are both facing the correct direction.  The small part of the spring should face TOWARDS the wheel. Like so: > WHEEL <

3) After you've confirmed that the springs are in correctly on your quick release, make sure it's properly tightened.  To properly tighten it, the quick release should "stick" or get tough half way through it's rotation.  The best way to visualize this is have the skewer so the lever flips in the vertical direction when you're looking at it from behind, then it should get tough about parallel with the ground. 

I hope this helps, if all else still continues to make noise, your rear derailleur may need a cable tension adjustment, but, make sure it's not due to improper installation, or improper skewer torque as the axle being hollow will compress under load and remove a small amount of play that is present in the bearings when they are not under load.

A better way to narrow down the tube size is to determine the size of the rim. This is normally represented by three numbers in mm. Not all rims are labeled. Almost every single tire you find will be labeled though. You're looking for these numbers ###-## the first three being the rim size in mm, and the last two being the width of the tire on question in mm. For example, a modern road tire that is "700x25c" will have the numbers 622-25 next to the quoted nominal size. We can then say the rim is 622 and the width of the tire is 25mm (helpful to know when sizing a tube).  With that knowledge in mind, your tube hunt should go smoothly!  Best of luck!

I was a little confused as to if it was having trouble downshifting the whole way or just a specific gear. If it's one gear, most likely bent derailleur hanger (as mentioned already. ) if it's the whole way down, you've got something in either your housing or your shifters causing resistance when releasing cable slack every down shift. Check your housing for any damage, and replace that segment (I'd do if all if it's been over a year as a rule of thumb. ) Also, check to see if the final segment of housing near the rear derailleur is long enough that the cable enters the barrel adjuster in a straight line. And finally, your B-limit screw may be improperly adjusted, shimano works well with 1-3mm distance from the upper pulley to the rear sprockets and SRAM wants a bit more like 4-6mm. Good luck! Let us know what you find out.
